rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly with no reported failures, so this candidate raises obfuscation intensity moderately while guarding the program's actual hot paths: Queens/Try are small recursive backtracking functions where control-flow obscuration pays off most, hence FLA and BCF get the highest SecurityGain, with FLA's RuntimeCost kept at 0.55 and BCF's SizeCost at 0.6 so the selector backs off on the tightest recursive loops rather than blanket-applying them. SUB stays cheap and near-universal (low cost/risk weights) since instruction substitution adds static-analysis friction with minimal overhead. IBR retains a high SecurityGain but its RuntimeCost is kept elevated (0.6) because indirect branches degrade branch prediction in the backtracking inner loop of Try; ICALL is kept mid-range since this 7-function program has few call sites to hide; IGV targets the board-state arrays and counters with moderate weights. All CorrectnessRisk weights remain at or above their round-0 levels relative to security gains so the demonstrated build-and-run correctness is preserved, and every pass is included since none caused failures in the measured round.
